title: Hybrid quota reset policy for reserved-capacity customers (calendar + rolling windows)
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Problem: Reserved capacity customers have two overlapping quota models: calendar-based monthly resets for committed units and rolling-window per-minute/per-hour throttles. We observed incorrect resets when customers used both reserved capacity and hosted burst capacity (edge case: calendar reset + active rolling counters). This ticket implements a unified policy that ensures predictable unit accounting and deterministic limits across both reset types.

Goals:
- Ensure monthly calendar quotas (committed reserved tokens) are reset at a single authoritative boundary without losing in-flight usage.
- Support rolling-window counters for short-term throttling that do not conflict with calendar reset semantics.
- Preserve billing accuracy for reserved customers (no double-counting or lost tokens).
- Provide migration path and visibility in Console (quota timeline + explanation).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Monthly reserved quotas reset exactly at configured calendar boundary (UTC midnight first-of-month) and there are no negative remaining units or duplicated deductions.
2) Rolling-window counters operate independently; short-term bursts during reset are correctly attributed to pre- or post-reset bucket per request timestamp.
3) Unit tests and integration tests simulate high-concurrency reset window and show consistent accounting.
4) Console shows a rendered timeline for affected customers for the last 72 hours including the reset event.
5) No regression in per-token billing for non-reserved customers.
6) Migration script completes within 10 minutes for tenants with >100M tokens historical counters (no downtime).
implementation_notes:
Design approach: introduce a two-tier quota ledger in our metering service. Ledger layers: 'calendar' ledger (month-granular, authoritative for committed capacity) and 'ephemeral' ledger (rolling counters used for throttles and transient bursts).

Key changes:
- Replace current single-counter reset hook with an ordered reset operation: 1) Pause writes to calendar ledger at reset boundary (short CAS window), 2) snapshot ephemeral ledger deltas and rebase them relative to the new calendar baseline, 3) atomically flip calendar pointer and resume writes.
- Use Redis streams + Lua scripts for atomic snapshot+rebase per-tenant to avoid race conditions at high QPS.
- Add idempotency keys for reset operations keyed by tenant_id+month to prevent double runs from orchestration retries.
- Update metering API to include 'usage_timestamp' in delta writes; use timestamp to attribute requests crossing the boundary.

Trade-offs considered:
- Option A (simpler): pause all request processing during reset for 30s. Rejected due to customer impact on SLAs.
- Option B (recommended): snapshot+rebase using optimistic CAS in Redis; slightly more complex but keeps latency unaffected.

Data migration: backfill calendar ledger for customers created prior to ledger launch using existing billing aggregates. Backfill will run in priority order (high-touch customers first).
testing_plan:
Unit tests: ledger snapshot/rebase logic, Lua atomic scripts, idempotency behavior.
Integration tests: simulate 10k rps tenant, run reset during sustained load, verify final counters against golden model.
Load tests: open-loop synthetic load with bursts around boundary.
Manual verification: run with a staging reserved tenant for a maintenance window and compare Console, billing exports, and raw ledgers.
Observability: add debug logging flags and a dashboard (grafana) showing reset duration, per-tenant rebase time, and conflict retry counts.
rollout_plan:
1) Feature-flag the new ledger implementation per-tenant.
2) Enable for a pilot group (5 reserved tenants) for 2 weeks, monitor fairness and billing diffs.
3) Gradually expand to all reserved customers over 2 maintenance windows.
4) Run backfill during off-peak hours with rate-limiting for DB writes.
5) Remove feature flag after 4 weeks if metrics stable and no billing discrepancies.

Rollback: revert feature flag and trigger idempotent compensating rebase using saved snapshots.
comments: 2026-02-12 - Aisha Khan: Initial triage. Reproduced issue in staging. Found case where ephemeral rolling counters were subtracted post calendar reset leading to negative remaining. Added failing regression test.

2026-02-13 - Diego Martinez: Spike completed. Verified Lua script approach can snapshot and rebase under 200ms for a tenant with 50k active keys. Draft PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4521

2026-02-15 - Lina Park (PM): Confirmed billing accuracy requirements with finance. Finance requires audit log entries for each reset and an exportable CSV of rebase operations per tenant. Added to acceptance criteria.
2026-02-17 - Security (notes): No KMS changes required. Reset operations must be logged to audit stream. Security sign-off not required but audit integration required.

2026-02-18 - QA: Found intermittent race where two reset jobs scheduled for same tenant cause duplicate idempotency key check failure. Fixed locking logic in orchestration scheduler. Updated tests to simulate duplicate schedulers.
2026-02-20 - Diego Martinez: Merged changes behind feature flag. Pilot enablement scripts ready. Next step: schedule pilot tenants and run backfill job.
